subject: Capacity squeeze / p99 jitter impacting ShopMart checkout - next steps
messages:
From: Meredith Lang <meredith@shopmart.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Checkout spikes today — p99 up, errors creeping in

Hi Aditya,

We started seeing intermittent slowdowns on our checkout flow this morning around 08:45 PDT. Our engineering dashboard shows p99 latency for the /checkout/generate endpoint jumping from ~0.7s to ~4.8s in short bursts, and a small uptick in 5xx errors (~0.6% -> 2.3%). This is affecting a few high-value orders.

I looked at the traces and attached a short p99-samples.log excerpt and a sparkline from our telemetry. Can you confirm whether this maps to capacity/queueing on your side or if we should look at our batching?

We need clarity fast — our ops lead has asked for a mitigation plan and whether you can route us to a more stable capacity tier.

Thanks,
Meredith
Meredith Lang
Head of Platform, ShopMart
meredith@shopmart.com

Subject: Re: Checkout spikes today — p99 up, errors creeping in

Hi Meredith — thanks for the data and flagging this. I’m looping in our on-call infra lead (Laura) and sales lead (Marcus). We’ll triage immediately.

High level: it sounds like a classic capacity-squeeze/queueing pattern — short bursts driving concurrency caps and KV cache churn. Laura, can you confirm if there were any scheduling anomalies or circuit breakers triggered for ShopMart this morning?

Next steps I propose now:
- Laura/eng: quick triage and confirm whether backpressure or a request-funneling policy hit.
- Sales: Marcus to provide short-term lift (burst capacity) and provide customer with ETA if we need to shift them to a reserved pool.
- Ops: I’ll coordinate a MAP (mutual action plan) and share a single doc.

Meredith — we’ll keep you posted on timelines; apologies for impact.

Aditya
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
[internal note: attaching MAP draft after eng confirms root cause]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-07-19T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Checkout spikes today — p99 up, errors creeping in

Aditya / Meredith — quick update from infra: we observed repeated short-lived request pileups from ShopMart’s key route between 08:42–09:05 PDT. Key signals:

- Concurrent inflight tokens for their customer key exceeded the configured soft cap for ~45s windows several times.
- Continuous batching combined with a sudden traffic fan-out caused KV cache churn (we saw increased small eviction rates), which amplified single-request latency for new contexts.
- Two automatic throttles fired (latency circuit and concurrency backoff) which led to request rejections and a small bump in 5xx.

Root cause (initial): a short traffic spike from a downstream partner that produced a fan-out of many small requests tying the same customer key, pushing them into the soft concurrency cap. That, plus cold-cache effects, caused p99 spikes.

Immediate mitigations we took (completed at 09:20 PDT):
- Raised soft concurrency cap for the ShopMart API key by 50% for 2 hours to let the burst drain.
- Temporarily disabled one of the conservative latency circuit thresholds for this key to avoid aggressive request rejections while we monitor.
- Enabled prefix/KV caching for their heavier prompt shapes for 4 hours.

Action items for the next 24 hours:
1) We will backfill longer traces and create a short MAP doc with timing and suggested permanent configuration changes.
2) Recommend ShopMart adopt a modest client-side jitter (100–300ms) and better request fan-in controls to avoid simultaneous requests on the same context.
3) Offer a reserved burst window or Dedicated lane if they expect repeated spikes.

I’m attaching a first-pass MAP (MAP-action-plan-v1.pdf) and the p99 log extract. We’ll follow with a more thorough root-cause and regression check.

Laura
Engineering Manager, Infra
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Checkout spikes today — p99 up, errors creeping in

Meredith — thanks for confirming receipt. From a commercial perspective, we want to reduce your operational risk while we finalize the technical remediation.

Proposed short-term options:
- Immediate: Grant a temporary burst credit for the next 48 hours and upgrade your plan to include a 2-hour reserved burst window (no billing increase during that window).
- Near-term: Evaluate Dedicated lane for peak checkout windows (we can run a 2-week pilot).

Aditya — please add a single-line summary for the customer-facing MAP that includes timeline, who owns each action, and the 48-hour credit. Meredith — if you want, we can schedule a 30-min post-mortem with your ops team and our infra leads this afternoon.

Marcus
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

[internal note: coordinate billing credit with finance after PM confirms issue is on our side]

Thanks team — the temporary cap raise and caching change made a big difference; p99 returned to ~0.8s and errors subsided overnight. Appreciate the burst credit offer — that should help for reconciliation.

We accepted the 30-min post-mortem today at 16:00 PDT. Topics we want: root cause timeline, recommended config changes (permanent cap increase? reserved pool?), and an outline of the Dedicated pilot.

See you all this afternoon.

— Meredith
